disease_label_per_paper: Thyroid storm presenting with cardiac arrest, cardiogenic shock, renal failure, and liver injury requiring VA-ECMO, CRRT, and plasma exchange
presentation_summary: 28-year-old man collapsed out of hospital with ventricular fibrillation cardiac arrest after an acute respiratory illness.
Family described about two months of heat intolerance, weight loss, hand tremors, and palpitations before presentation.
After 60 minutes of resuscitation and ROSC, ED findings included temperature 40.5 C, heart rate 155/min, blood pressure 146/83 mmHg, GCS 3, and severe thyrotoxicosis with undetectable TSH.
He developed severe thyrotoxic cardiomyopathy/cardiogenic shock, anuric acute kidney injury needing CRRT, and worsening transaminitis.
Despite thionamide, iodine, glucocorticoid, cooling, VA-ECMO, CRRT, and therapeutic plasma exchange, care was withdrawn after diffuse cerebral edema and tonsillar herniation.

clinical_course.event: Heat intolerance, weight loss, tremor, and palpitations were present for about two months before collapse.
Out-of-hospital ventricular fibrillation arrest with ROSC after 60 minutes of resuscitation.
Initial investigations included elevated inflammatory markers, mixed respiratory and metabolic acidosis, raised troponin I, and normal electrolyte levels.
NG propylthiouracil, IV sodium iodide, hydrocortisone, cooling blanket, and low-dose esmolol were started.
Low-dose esmolol was followed by pulseless electrical activity arrest, then vasopressors, VA-ECMO, and CRRT were required.
Therapeutic plasma exchange was used for hormone removal while multiorgan support continued.
Neuroimaging showed diffuse cerebral edema with tonsillar herniation and care was withdrawn.
